page: Amazon Web Services r6in.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the configuration supplies 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 54 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic and vector processing. The instance features 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation suited for data footprints exceeding standard compute distributions.

Network throughput is provisioned at a 75 Gbps baseline, facilitating rapid data movement for cluster-wide communications and external data transfers. The instance does not include bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage options like Amazon Elastic Block Store. Standardized benchmark testing shows strong execution in cryptographic and image transformations, with PassMark CPU encryption reaching 43,336.17 and Geekbench image processing reaching 14,701.0, both placing in the top quartile. General compute and memory bandwidth reflect middle-tier performance, producing 161.35 GB/s uncached memory read bandwidth and 49.56 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6in.12xlarge offers high memory density and enterprise network bandwidth in a balanced virtualized envelope. Because local NVMe disks are omitted, storage I/O profiles depend entirely on network storage configurations. The instance is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed Redis caching, big data ETL processing, and transactional database environments that demand high memory capacity per core.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) clocked at 3.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 54 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instructions. Network bandwidth is provisioned at a baseline of 75 Gbps, while local instance storage is absent, requiring Amazon EBS for persistence. In benchmark evaluations, the instance achieves top-quartile results in PassMark CPU encryption and Geekbench image processing, alongside 49.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 161.35 GB/s uncached memory read bandwidth. With high network bandwidth and substantial memory density, the r6in.12xlarge fits distributed caching clusters, large in-memory databases, and high-throughput memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
